compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`_CASCADING_EDGES` (`src/rebar/_commands/transition.py`) maps each cascading child edge to
**exactly one** eligible parent status. That shape covers the common case but leaves
reachable states that still violate I4a's stated invariant, "A child never runs ahead of
its parent in the lifecycle" (`docs/concurrency.md` §I4a).

Two concrete residuals, both observed while fixing `paragonite-fruited-minnow`
(96db-365e-f2c3-4547):

1. **`closed -> in_progress` under an OPEN parent.** The entry is
   `("closed","in_progress") -> "closed"`, so only a `closed` parent is eligible. Reactivate
   a closed child whose parent is merely `open` and you get `child=in_progress` under
   `parent=open` — the very state the `open -> in_progress` edge exists to prevent. Pinned
   today as intended by
   `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py::test_reactivate_does_not_disturb_open_parent`,
   which matches minnow's AC2 ("an already-`in_progress` or `open` parent is not disturbed")
   — so the current behaviour is deliberate for that ticket's scope, and this ticket asks
   whether the scope was right.
2. **`blocked -> in_progress` (a blocked resume).** Not in the table at all, so resuming a
   blocked child under an `open` or `closed` parent cascades nothing. Note the start-work
   GATE already fires on this edge (`transition_compute` keys the gate on the TARGET
   status, task 65e3 / stab-bunch-foyer), so the gate and the cascade disagree about which
   edges count as "starting work".

## Why this is one ticket, not two
Both are the same shape of gap: the table is keyed edge -> one status, while the invariant
is really "the parent must not be BEHIND the child", which is a comparison over a status
ordering. Fixing either one properly probably means replacing the single eligible status
with an ordering predicate (`idea < open < in_progress`, with `closed`/`blocked` handled
explicitly) rather than adding more one-off rows.

## Caution (scope rule)
Any change here must not make a previously-REFUSED transition succeed. Widening what the
cascade PULLS is restoration of a documented invariant; widening what a transition PERMITS
is not, and `claim`'s refusal of non-`open` tickets in particular is deliberate
(`txn.claim_core`) and must stay.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A decision is recorded on whether I4a's invariant is enforced by an ordering
      predicate or by an enumerated edge table.
- [ ] Reactivating a closed child under an `open` parent either cascades, or `docs/concurrency.md`
      §I4a explicitly documents the residual as accepted, with the reason.
- [ ] `blocked -> in_progress` either cascades, or is explicitly documented as non-cascading
      alongside the note that the start-work gate DOES fire on it.
- [ ] No transition that is refused today becomes permitted; the claim-status guard is untouched.
compiled_state.title: Cascade table's one-eligible-status-per-edge shape leaves I4a states reachable
